purpose: The CLOSED registry of semantic-identity exclusions of the population owner: a declaration listed here does not count as that family's authored position on that axis. An entry is bound to one family, one axis, one skin file and the exact rule it was reviewed with: its at-rule context (an empty list means a top-level rule), selector, property and value, whitespace-normalized, comments removed. It acts on the byProperty derivation only; a head-channel read is never excluded. A declaration that changes value, gains a channel, is repeated under the same selector, moves under an at-rule or moves to another part no longer matches and the family re-enters the axis by itself.

entries.reason: semantic identity: the legend marker is a 3px stroke segment and its radius is the HTML rendition of a line-cap, a quantity of the chart grammar's marks posture (data-chart-marks), not a corner of a box. The value is not a rung: it is the literal full end of the ramp, which the dial does not scale (--ds-radius-full is 9999px in every vertical, bithire 0.8 included), and on a 3px box every radius above 1.5px paints the same pill. No shape decision in the catalog may lawfully move this declaration. The plotted line is SVG (stroke-linecap), which kit rule 4 does not count as shape. --_ds-line-marker-radius has no producer at the reviewed commit; the fallback always paints. The skeleton-bar dome (`999px 999px 0 0` on `[data-part='skeleton-bar']`, a flex-sized bar in the scaffold's four-bar row) is saturated by its own box: CSS clamps adjacent radii to the box, so every radius at or above half the bar's inline size paints the same semicircle, and `--ds-radius-full` (9999px in every vertical) would paint identically. The literal is therefore the full end of the ramp, not a rung, and no catalog shape decision could move a pixel of it. Whether rottay's technical-sharp marks want a dome at all is the same marks-lane follow-up registered for the legend cap.

entries.reason: semantic identity: the pie's mark is a circle, so its legend marker is a circle and its loading placeholder is a donut ring (aspect-ratio 1, radial-gradient), the chart's own silhouette while it loads. 50% is the circle itself, not a rung: below 50% (37.5% at the dial's 0.75 floor) it is a rounded square, and above 50% CSS clamps it back to the circle, so the dial could only ever deform it, never govern it. No shape decision may lawfully move these two radii without breaking what the marker and the placeholder mean. The slices are SVG paths, which kit rule 4 does not count as shape. --_ds-pie-marker-radius has no producer at the reviewed commit; the fallback always paints.

entries.reason: semantic identity: the divider is a 2px stroke, a vertical hairline with a paper highlight, and its 1px radius is the stroke's end-cap, the HTML rendition of a line-cap on a 2px line, not a corner of a box. 1px is half the authored inline-size, so it is the box's own geometry and not a rung: on this box every radius from 1px to the full rung paints the same pixels (1px, 1.15px, 1.25px, 2px and 9999px are hash-identical at 1x, 2x and 3x, because the browser clamps a radius to half the box), while below half the cap opens into a rounded rectangle (0.75px, the dial's floor, and 0.8px repaint). A radius-scale dial-up would therefore be credited by the probe as a computed-style move with no paint behind it, and a dial-down would break the mark. The radius-scale dial does not scale the full rung (--ds-radius-full is the constant 9999px in every vertical) and this cap reads no channel of any shape row. It is the only shape declaration the skin authors. No shape decision may lawfully move this radius without breaking what the mark is. The premise is the 2px inline-size authored in the same rule, pinned in the population tests; a box change returns the entry to review.
